exposure: Observation group (evidence-based nursing plus diet nursing)
Control group (routine nursing plus diet nursing)
outcome: Blood glucose index (fasting blood glucose, 2 h postprandial blood glucose, HbA1c)
Intestinal flora (Bifidobacterium, Lactobacillus, Bifidobacterium to E. coli ratio)
Pregnancy outcome (pregnancy infection rate, cesarean section rate, premature delivery rate, polyhydramnios rate)
Perinatal outcome (macrosomia, neonatal hypoglycemia, neonatal hyperbilirubinemia, fetal malformation rate, neonatal asphyxia rate)
cohort: 130 patients with gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) admitted to a hospital in China
finding: The study found that evidence-based care combined with dietary care in GDM patients can improve intestinal flora, control blood glucose, improve patient compliance behavior, and improve maternal and infant outcomes compared to routine care plus diet nursing.
mod_finding: The cesarean section rate was significantly lower in the observation group (evidence-based care combined with dietary care) compared to the control group.
